Marissa / Emily — attaching the artifacts we can share immediately. See attachments (stubs listed below) and notes on redaction/coverage.

Attachments included (redwood internal copies):
- redwood-sso-saml-metadata.xml (SAML metadata file; contains entityID and IdP/SP endpoints)
- redwood-scim-provisioning-log-2026-02.csv (Provisioning events CSV, user ids hashed, timestamps in UTC)
- redwood-rbac-role-matrix-2026-03.pdf (Role matrix, includes service-level permissions)

Key notes:
- SSO: We enforce SAML2.0 with required NameID and groups claim. We require IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows only over HTTPS; metadata file is current as of 2026-03-01. Multi-factor auth is enforced via customer-managed IdP (we can supply MFA policy reference on request).
- SCIM: Our provisioning engine emits event records for create/update/deactivate to the SCIM endpoint. The CSV contains event_type, target_hash, actor, and timestamp. We have rate limits but no batching loss; deltas are handled via standard SCIM PATCH semantics.
- RBAC: The attached PDF lists canonical roles (admin, workspace_admin, engineer, read_only) mapped to API scopes. Role assignment changes are audited; example audit row (redacted) included in the CSV: timestamp, actor, action, target_role.
- Least privilege: We run role reviews quarterly and apply permission scoping by default to workspace-level resources; service-to-service calls use short-lived tokens with scoped scopes.

Redaction / sharing constraints: Laura has confirmed we must hash user identifiers in logs for external distribution and remove customer-provided PII. The CSV attached has hashed user IDs and does not include email addresses. For reviewers who need raw logs under NDA, we can set up a secure viewing session.

If anything else is needed (SAML assertion example, more granular audit logs), say the word and we can arrange an internal security call.

-rishi
